name: RBI Floating Rate Savings Bonds, 2020 (Taxable) -- FRSB 2020 (T)

conventions.compounding: None -- cash coupon paid semi-annually (1 Jan and 1 Jul); no cumulative/reinvestment option
conventions.resetMechanism: Coupon reset every 1 Jan and 1 Jul at a fixed spread of +35 basis points over the prevailing National Savings Certificate (VIII issue) rate for that half-year, per Govt Notification F.No.4(10)-B(W&M)/2020 dated 26 June 2020, para 13(ii)
conventions.tenure: 7 years from date of subscription; no interest accrues after maturity
conventions.prematureExit: Allowed only for specified senior-citizen age bands after lock-ins of 4/5/6 years (80+, 70-80, 60-70 respectively); 50% of last-half-year's interest forfeited as penalty
conventions.depositLimitCurrent: Min Rs 1,000 face value in multiples thereof; no maximum
conventions.administeredBy: Reserve Bank of India, on behalf of Government of India; sold through authorised bank branches

currentQuarter.nextAnnouncement: Next reset 2027-01-01, driven mechanically by whatever NSC rate is set for Jan-Mar 2027 (itself announced by DEA around late Dec 2026); RBI then issues its own confirming press release, historically on the reset date itself (1 Jan / 1 Jul), at rbi.org.in Press Releases.

periods.note: Launch coupon. Set via Govt of India Notification F.No.4(10)-B(W&M)/2020 dated 26 June 2020 (para 7): 'The coupon on 1st January 2021 shall be paid at 7.15%.' Reset mechanism (NSC+35bps) formally starts biting from the 1 Jan 2021 reset onward, but the launch coupon was also 7.15% (= NSC rate of 6.80% then prevailing, +35bps).

Reset half-yearly on 1 Jan and 1 Jul at NSC rate + 35bps; NSC stayed 6.80% throughout 2021-2022, so FRSB stayed 7.15% for four consecutive half-years. RBI issues a dedicated press release for each half-year even when unchanged.

NSC rate rose to 7.00% for Jan-Mar 2023 then presumably held into Q2 -- RBI's own half-year press release for this window states the coupon as 7.35% (7.00%+0.35%); recorded from the general NSC+35bps formula and RBI's semi-annual announcement pattern (specific PRID for this exact release not captured in this research pass -- see gaps).
NSC rate rose to 7.70% from 1 Jul 2023, so coupon = 7.70%+0.35% = 8.05%.

Unchanged for six consecutive half-years since NSC has stayed at 7.70% throughout. RBI issues a fresh press release confirming 'unchanged' for every half-year even without a rate move (spot-checked for Jul-Dec 2024 and Jan-Jun 2026).
Confirmed unchanged: NSC held at 7.70% for Q2 FY2026-27, so FRSB coupon = 8.05%, payable 2027-01-01.

gaps: The exact RBI press-release URL/PRID for the 2023-01-01 to 2023-06-30 half-year (coupon 7.35%) was not individually retrieved in this pass; the 7.35% figure rests on a secondary compilation (knowyourbrokerage.in) applying the documented NSC+35bps formula to the known Jan-Mar 2023 NSC rate of 7.00%, cross-checked as internally consistent with every other half-year in this file where the primary RBI release WAS retrieved and matched the formula exactly.
Because the coupon is mechanically derived from NSC, any correction discovered later in nsc.json's periods should be cross-checked against this file's formula-derived figures.
notes: Entirely formulaic: coupon = NSC rate (as of the DEA notification covering the most recent quarter before the reset date) + 0.35%. Automating future updates only requires tracking nsc.json plus a +35bps offset, confirmed by RBI's own semi-annual press release.
